run.question: What arrangement could James become relevant to as a safeguarding / child-protection / trauma-informed trainer for international schools operating in Africa?
run.summary: Strong independent discovery: international-school safeguarding training. COBIS + CIS verified as bodies that procure recurring safeguarding/safer-recruitment training via external experts. James = UK safeguarding DSL + developmental trauma + ICPC-checkable + Accra. Gaps: named safeguarding lead + day rate.

hypotheses.statement: These bodies use only in-house or UK-based trainers, so James has no entry (UNVERIFIED - the COBIS line about collaborating with global experts argues against this)
International schools/school groups in Africa need recurring safeguarding and child-protection staff training and will pay a trainer who knows the UK framework AND the West African context

propositions.title: External safeguarding / child-protection trainer for international schools in West Africa
propositions.arrangement: COBIS / CIS (and the BISSC coalition bodies) deliver recurring safeguarding and safer-recruitment training to member schools; James is engaged as the West Africa-based external trainer who delivers it to schools in the region
propositions.james_role: Delivers UK-standard safeguarding, child-protection and trauma-informed (developmental trauma) training to international-school staff in West Africa; knows both the UK framework and the local context; ICPC-checkable (lived in UK)
propositions.value_to_them: Recurring, compliant safeguarding training for all staff, delivered by someone who understands both the UK framework and the West African context, without flying a UK trainer in each time
propositions.counterfactual: Without James they either fly in a UK safeguarding trainer (costly, no local context) or use a local educator without the UK safeguarding framework; James is the bridge and is based in Accra

economics.who_pays: COBIS / CIS / member school groups (BISSC bodies: AoBSO, BSME, FOBISIA, LAHC, NABSS) - to confirm direct contract vs via school group
economics.amount_range: ESTIMATE ONLY - specialist safeguarding-trainer day rate; not yet verified against market
economics.timing: per training engagement, annual staff-training cycle
economics.net_estimate: To be confirmed once rate is verified
economics.basis: No verified rate found; comparable external safeguarding-trainer engagements in international education need a market check. Flagged as estimate, not fact.

propositions.uncertainties: No named safeguarding lead verified yet; whether COBIS/CIS contract trainers directly or route via school groups; actual day rate; any required trainer accreditation
propositions.invalidators: If they use only in-house or UK-based trainers and will not engage regional external experts; if a specific certification James lacks is mandatory
propositions.next_step: Conversation with COBIS (and CIS) about their stated pathway to collaborate with global experts on safeguarding training, and whether they need a West Africa-based trainer
propositions.decision_reasoning: Verified: COBIS (350 British international schools, 86 countries) and CIS both run safeguarding/child-protection training and safer-recruitment programmes; COBIS states it collaborates with global experts to deliver training and is ICPC Global Ambassador + founding member of the International Task Force on Child Protection and BISSC. James is a UK-trained Deputy Safeguarding Lead with developmental-trauma expertise, ICPC-checkable, Accra-based. Strong counterfactual. Main gap: no named safeguarding lead and unverified day rate.

evidence.excerpt: Council of British International Schools: 350 member schools, 86 countries, 262,000 students, 25,500 teachers; dedicated Safeguarding, Accreditation, Professional Learning and Training services; unfaltering commitment to safeguarding and child protection; London +44 20 3826 7190
evidence.supports_claim: British international schools across 86 countries (incl. Africa) have a structured safeguarding-training need served by a membership body

evidence.excerpt: COBIS offers online and face-to-face Safeguarding Training for all staff; Safer Recruitment; is ICPC Global Ambassador; founding member of the International Task Force on Child Protection and the British International Schools Safeguarding Coalition (AoBSO, BSME, FOBISIA, LAHC, NABSS). States: we collaborate with global experts to deliver tailored training programmes for all school staff
evidence.supports_claim: British international-school bodies use external expert trainers to deliver recurring safeguarding training to member schools across many countries incl. Africa

evidence.excerpt: Council of International Schools: core service areas include Child Protection and Child Protection & Well-being; runs an Affiliated Consultant Network and Affiliated School Groups; active International Safer Recruitment programme
evidence.supports_claim: International-school bodies actively procure child-protection and safer-recruitment training via networks of external consultants

decisions.reasoning: Verified: COBIS (350 British international schools, 86 countries) and CIS both run safeguarding/child-protection training and safer-recruitment programmes; COBIS states it collaborates with global experts to deliver training and is ICPC Global Ambassador + founding member of the International Task Force on Child Protection and BISSC. James is a UK-trained Deputy Safeguarding Lead with developmental-trauma expertise, ICPC-checkable, Accra-based. Strong counterfactual. Main gap: no named safeguarding lead and unverified day rate.
